:::{#def-gradient-ascent}
#### Gradient ascent

Let $f : \reals^p \to \reals$ have first [partial derivatives](vector-calculus.qmd#def-partial-derivative),
let $\vx^{(0)}$ be a starting point,
and let $s^{(0)}, s^{(1)}, \ldots$ be positive [step lengths](#def-gradient-descent).
**Gradient ascent**
[@wikipedia_gradient_descent]
repeats, for $t = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$, the update

$$
\vx^{(t+1)} \eqdef \vx^{(t)} + s^{(t)}\,\deriv{\vx} f(\vx^{(t)}).
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-gradient-ascent}
#### Gradient ascent is gradient descent on the negative function

Gradient ascent on $f$ takes the same steps as [gradient descent](#def-gradient-descent) on $-f$,
since $\deriv{\vx} (-f) = -\deriv{\vx} f$.
In one variable, for $f(x) = -x^2$ the [derivative](calculus.qmd#def-derivative) is $f'(x) = -2x$, so gradient ascent with fixed [step length](#def-gradient-descent) $s$ is
$x^{(t+1)} = (1 - 2s)\,x^{(t)}$,
the iteration of @exm-gradient-descent, which tends to the maximizer $0$ when $0 < s < 1$.

:::
